dialog.body: Utilities billing, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hi, yes, good morning. My name is Theresa Cirelli, and I'm calling about a water and sewer bill. I'm on speaker, I've got my hands full, so I hope you can hear me okay.
I can hear you fine. Go ahead, Ms. Cirelli.

Okay, so let me start from last week, because that's when this started for me. Last Tuesday I got an email, a reminder, saying I had an overdue balance on my water account. And I thought, what overdue balance? I never got a bill. Not one.
Okay. What's the service address on the account?

125 Marsh Street, down in the Point. It's my shop, well, it's my business space. So Wednesday, that was the next day, I dug through everything, and nothing from the city. Thursday I finally logged into the online portal and looked, and the mailing address on the account is my old one. From before I moved the business. So the bill has been going to some address where I haven't been for, I don't know, over a year.
I see. So the billing address on file is out of date, and the notices have been going there.
Right. And nobody told me. I only found out because of the reminder, which, honestly, if that hadn't come I'd still have no idea.
Let me pull up the account. Can you give me the account number, or just the service address is fine?
I have the address. I don't have the number in front of me, I'm in the back and the paperwork's up front.

That's fine, the address will do. [pause] Okay, I have 125 Marsh Street. I do see the mailing address is different from the service address, and there's an open balance. It looks like a couple of billing cycles.
A couple. Okay. And is there a penalty on it? Because I'd be annoyed if I'm getting charged late fees on a bill I never saw.

I can see there's a late charge noted on the older one. I can't tell you what happens with it yet. I can note that the notices went to the wrong address and have that reviewed. Was the address change ever submitted to us?
I thought it was. When I moved I filled out something, I think with the business license people. I figured it all got passed along. Apparently not.
Those are separate offices, so it may not have carried over. I can update the mailing address right now if you give me the correct one.
Yes, please. Just send it to the shop. 125 Marsh Street. Same as the service address.
Got it. I've changed the mailing address to 125 Marsh Street. You should get the next bill there.
Good. Now here's the other thing. Looking at the amount, it says estimated. Estimated reading. Why is it estimated?
Let me look at that. [pause] It shows the last few readings as estimates. There's a note that the meter couldn't be accessed.

Yeah, so, the meter is in a crawlspace under the back part of the building. Nobody goes in there. I haven't been in there in years, it's tight, there's no light. I don't think anyone from the city has been in there either.

That would explain it. If the reader can't get to it, the system estimates based on past usage. We can request a visit to access the meter, or look at whether there's an option for a reading device outside. I'd need to send that to the meter team.
Can you do that? Put in the request? Because I don't want to keep paying on guesses.
Yes, I'll put in a request. They'll probably want to call you to arrange access, so is the number on the account a good one?
It's 401-555-0157. That's my cell. It's the best one.
Thank you, I've got that, 401-555-0157. I'll add it to the request.

Okay. Now, what I want to do is just pay what's due so it stops being overdue. But I'm at the shop till late, and I'm usually here after City Hall closes. Can I pay it online tonight? Like after hours, once you're closed?
Yes, the online payment portal is available around the clock. You can pay tonight, any time. There's also a drop box at City Hall for checks if you'd rather do that.
Online is fine. Will it show right away, though? Because the reminder said something about shutoff.

A payment made online generally posts quickly, and I'm adding a note to the account now that you've contacted us today about the address problem. I can't promise how the late charge will be handled, but the note will be there.
Fine. So, just so I have it in order. You changed my mailing address, you're putting in a request about the meter in the crawlspace, you noted the account, and I can pay tonight on the website.
That's right. You may want to check the portal tomorrow to make sure the payment shows and the address is updated.
Okay. Sorry, I'm a little short, I've just been chasing this all week. I'm in the middle of a project here, I build model trains in the spare room, and I lost half of Thursday to this.
No need to apologize. It's frustrating to find out about a bill that way. Is there anything else I can help with?
No, that's it. Thanks, Priya.
You're welcome. Have a good day.
